svg.title: The information ladder — what each privilege buys, in clears per move
svg.desc: A four-rung ladder ordered by privilege, with rung height equal to measured numbered clears per move. Bottom rung: fair depth-4 expectimax, no sampling, public state only — 1.9865 on 128 fresh tapes (finding-12), with a dashed ghost rung at its inflated eight-tape reading 2.0467 (finding-06 section 2). Next: arm B, the legal fair planner with hidden board and future both sampled (H=7, K=256) — 2.0260 on 32 fresh tapes (finding-12 section 2), with a dashed ghost at the withdrawn eight-tape reading 2.2309 (finding-07 section 1) and a downward correction arrow. Next: arm A, future tape known but hidden board sampled (K=64) — 2.1361 on the eight master tapes (finding-07 section 2), never re-run fresh. Top: the clairvoyant rh-clears H=7, hidden board and future tape known — 2.3663 on 64 fresh tapes (finding-12 section 6). A dashed line at 2.400 = 12/5 marks the exact survival requirement (finding-01). Arrows between rungs carry the recorded shares: fair planning of this kind closes +0.1256 = 27.1% of the matched-cohort gap (corrected; finding-07 printed 58.8%, withdrawn), knowing the future tape is worth about 0% (2.1361 vs 2.1403 at K=64), and 72.9% is not closed — hidden board plus hindsight-optimization suboptimality, an upper bound. Rung heights mix cohorts (best available per rung); the shares come from the matched 32-fresh-tape cohort (D4 1.9004, arm B 2.0260, clairvoyant 2.3637). Sources: docs/exploratory/finding-06-flow-ceiling.md, finding-07-fair-planning-ceiling.md, finding-12-fair-planner-ceiling-extended.md, finding-01-score-is-survival.md.
svg.text: The information ladder — what each privilege buys, in clears per move
findings 06 → 07 → 12: separating planning from hidden information (with the fresh-tape correction)
numbered clears per move (whole game) — rung height
clairvoyant rh-clears H=7 — hidden board + tape known
arm A — tape known, hidden board sampled (K=64)
arm B — both sampled: a legal policy (H=7, K=256)
rung height = measured clears per move; rungs are ordered by privilege — what the evaluator may see.
solid rungs: fresh-tape cohorts · dashed rungs: the eight master tapes finding-12 showed favour long games

g.title: Clairvoyant rung — both privileges
g.text: i
rh-clears H=7: reads the hidden board AND the future tape; an exact
7-move window solved every move. 2.3663 clears / 1.3832 reveals per move
on 64 fresh tapes; 59 of 64 games censored alive at the cap
(finding-12 §6). A ceiling and teacher, never a deployable policy.
On the matched 32-tape cohort it measures 2.3637 (finding-12 §2).

g.title: Arm A — tape known, board sampled
g.text: i
Arm A: the future disc tape is known, the hidden board is sampled (K=64).
2.1361 clears/move on the eight master tapes (finding-07 §2). At matched
K=64, arm B scored 2.1403 — the tape bought −0.004: knowing the future
is worth nothing to this planner. Never re-run on fresh tapes, so this
rung keeps its eight-tape dash.

g.title: Arm B ghost — the withdrawn reading
g.text: i
Withdrawn reading: 2.2309 on the eight master tapes (finding-07 §1).
finding-12 showed those tapes favour long games; the same configuration
measures 2.0260 on 32 fresh tapes. The ghost rung keeps the correction
visible — the arrow next to it is the fresh-tape correction.

g.title: Arm B — the legal planner
g.text: i
Arm B: hidden board and future both sampled — a legal policy reading
public state only. H=7, K=256: 2.0260 clears / 1.1256 reveals per move on
32 fresh tapes (finding-12 §2). Every fair game still ended — 0 of 160
fresh-tape fair games survived (finding-07 correction notice; finding-12).
Legal by construction; expensive: 256 exact window solves per move.

g.title: Fair D4 ghost — the inflated baseline
g.text: i
Ghost: fair D4's eight-tape reading, 2.0467 (finding-06 §2) — inflated;
the same configuration measures 1.9865 on 128 fresh tapes (finding-12).
The correction shrinks the baseline, which enlarges the true gap by 21%
and halves the planning share of it.

g.title: Fair D4 — the reference
g.text: i
Fair depth-4 expectimax: no sampling, public state only, the program's
reference. 1.9865 clears/move on 128 fresh tapes; 1.9004 on the 32-tape
matched subset used for the decomposition (finding-12 §2). Eight-tape
reading 2.0467 (finding-06 §2), shown as the ghost rung above.

g.title: Fair planning closes 27.1% (corrected)
g.text: i
Closed by fair planning at H=7, K=256: +0.1256 clears/move = 27.1% of the
matched-cohort gap (finding-12 §2; matched arms on 32 fresh tapes: D4
1.9004, arm B 2.0260, clairvoyant 2.3637). finding-07 printed 58.8% —
withdrawn: D4's baseline was cohort-inflated, the clairvoyant ceiling not.
At H=5 the corrected share is 22.2% (15.3% against the all-128 denominator).

g.title: Not closed — 72.9%, an upper bound
g.text: i
Not closed: 0.3377 = 72.9% of the matched-cohort gap (finding-12 §2).
An upper bound on hidden information; it also contains PIMC's structural
blindness to acting in order to learn — valuing reveals is the named,
actionable residual (finding-07 §2 and §6; the game demands 1.400
covered reveals per move by the same conservation law).

g.title: Knowing the tape — about zero
g.text: i
Knowing the future disc tape: ≈0% of the gap — arm A 2.1361 vs arm B
2.1403 at K=64 on the eight tapes (finding-07 §2). A determinized planner
is not monotone in information: fixing the tape removes sample diversity
and sharpens strategy fusion (see diagram-strategy-fusion).

g.title: The survival requirement
g.text: i
2.400 = 12/5 numbered clears per move — exact disc conservation
(finding-01). Whole-game clairvoyant rates sit just under it because of
the sparse opening; the steady-state second half reaches 2.4023
(finding-06 §2.1).
